claim: Age-associated DNA methylation in blood cells convey information on health status.
source: Age-associated DNA methylation in blood cells convey information on health status.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general premise of the study.

claim: The mechanisms that drive age-associated DNA methylation changes in circulating cells and their relationships to gene regulation are unknown.
source: However, the mechanisms that drive these changes in circulating cells and their relationships to gene regulation are unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the abstract.

claim: Of the thousands of age-associated sites, only 350 sites were differentially methylated in the same direction in all cell types.
source: Of the thousands of age-associated sites, only 350 sites were differentially methylated in the same direction in all cell types and validated in an independent longitudinal cohort.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract based on the study's data analysis.

claim: The 350 age-associated sites differentially methylated in all cell types were validated in an independent longitudinal cohort.
source: Of the thousands of age-associated sites, only 350 sites were differentially methylated in the same direction in all cell types and validated in an independent longitudinal cohort.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data from the InCHIANTI study.

claim: Genes close to age-associated hypomethylated sites were enriched for collagen biosynthesis and complement cascade pathways.
source: Genes close to age-associated hypomethylated sites were enriched for collagen biosynthesis and complement cascade pathways, while genes close to hypermethylated sites mapped to neuronal pathways.
evidence: This is a finding from pathway enrichment analysis reported in the abstract.

claim: Genes close to age-associated hypermethylated sites mapped to neuronal pathways.
source: Genes close to age-associated hypomethylated sites were enriched for collagen biosynthesis and complement cascade pathways, while genes close to hypermethylated sites mapped to neuronal pathways.
evidence: This is a finding from pathway enrichment analysis reported in the abstract.

claim: In most cell types, the age-associated hypomethylated sites were enriched for ARNT (HIF1β) transcription factor motifs.
source: In silico analyses showed that in most cell types, the age-associated hypo- and hypermethylated sites were enriched for ARNT (HIF1β) and REST transcription factor (TF) motifs, respectively, which are both master regulators of hypoxia response.
evidence: This is a finding from in silico TF motif analysis reported in the abstract.

claim: In most cell types, the age-associated hypermethylated sites were enriched for REST transcription factor motifs.
source: In silico analyses showed that in most cell types, the age-associated hypo- and hypermethylated sites were enriched for ARNT (HIF1β) and REST transcription factor (TF) motifs, respectively, which are both master regulators of hypoxia response.
evidence: This is a finding from in silico TF motif analysis reported in the abstract.

claim: ARNT (HIF1β) and REST are both master regulators of hypoxia response.
source: In silico analyses showed that in most cell types, the age-associated hypo- and hypermethylated sites were enriched for ARNT (HIF1β) and REST transcription factor (TF) motifs, respectively, which are both master regulators of hypoxia response.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about these transcription factors.

claim: DNA methylation changes in healthy aging may be adaptive responses to fluctuations of oxygen availability.
source: These features suggest that DNA methylation changes in healthy aging may be adaptive responses to fluctuations of oxygen availability.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the enrichment of hypoxia-related TF motifs.

claim: Epigenetic clocks closely approximate chronological age.
source: Epigenetic clocks closely approximate chronological age and beyond age, predict adverse health conditions, including frailty (Gale et al., 2018), Alzheimer's disease (McCartney et al., 2018), and mortality (Marioni et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Epigenetic clocks predict adverse health conditions, including frailty.
source: Epigenetic clocks closely approximate chronological age and beyond age, predict adverse health conditions, including frailty (Gale et al., 2018), Alzheimer's disease (McCartney et al., 2018), and mortality (Marioni et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gale et al., 2018.

claim: Epigenetic clocks predict Alzheimer's disease.
source: Epigenetic clocks closely approximate chronological age and beyond age, predict adverse health conditions, including frailty (Gale et al., 2018), Alzheimer's disease (McCartney et al., 2018), and mortality (Marioni et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to McCartney et al., 2018.

claim: Epigenetic clocks predict mortality.
source: Epigenetic clocks closely approximate chronological age and beyond age, predict adverse health conditions, including frailty (Gale et al., 2018), Alzheimer's disease (McCartney et al., 2018), and mortality (Marioni et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Marioni et al., 2015 and Chen et al., 2016.

claim: Changes in DNA methylation with aging are regulated by specific mechanisms rather than by a stochastic drift.
source: Research suggest that changes in DNA methylation with aging are regulated by specific mechanisms rather than by a stochastic drift (Teschendorff et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Teschendorff et al., 2013.

claim: A loss-of-function mutation in the H3K36 histone methyltransferase has been associated with epigenetic aging in mice.
source: For example, a loss-of-function mutation in the H3K36 histone methyltransferase has been associated with epigenetic aging in mice (Martin-Herranz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Martin-Herranz et al., 2019.

claim: Polymorphisms in the telomerase gene (TERT) have been related to accelerated aging in humans.
source: In humans, polymorphisms in the telomerase gene (TERT) (Lu et al., 2018) and age-dependent gain of methylation in the Polycomb repressive complex 2 have been related to accelerated aging (Teschendorff et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lu et al., 2018.

claim: Age-dependent gain of methylation in the Polycomb repressive complex 2 has been related to accelerated aging in humans.
source: In humans, polymorphisms in the telomerase gene (TERT) (Lu et al., 2018) and age-dependent gain of methylation in the Polycomb repressive complex 2 have been related to accelerated aging (Teschendorff et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Teschendorff et al., 2010.

claim: No sound hypothesis exists that explains the association of DNA methylation with aging and pathology.
source: However, so far, no sound hypothesis exists that explains the association of DNA methylation with aging and pathology.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the introduction.

claim: Most human studies on age-associated DNA methylation were performed in mixed blood cell types.
source: A main obstacle in understanding mechanisms driving age-associated changes of DNA methylation is that most human studies were performed in mixed blood cell types.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of previous research.

claim: Previous studies that investigated select immune circulating cells failed to propose a unifying biological hypothesis explaining predictable changes of DNA methylation with aging.
source: The few studies that investigated select immune circulating cells failed to propose a unifying biological hypothesis explaining predictable changes of DNA methylation with aging (Dozmorov et al., 2017; Reynolds et al., 2014; Tserel et al., 2015; Bell et al., 2012; Kananen et al., 2016; Acevedo et al., 2015; Marttila et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: The study analyzed age-associated methylation in six purified blood-borne cell types sorted from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 55 donors of ages ranging from 22 to 83 years.
source: We analyzed age-associated methylation in six purified blood-borne cell types sorted from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 55 donors of ages ranging from 22 to 83 years.
evidence: This describes the study design and sample characteristics.

claim: Participants were ascertained to be healthy by trained health professionals according to strict clinical criteria.
source: To minimize the confounding of age-associated pre-clinical and clinical diseases, participants were ascertained to be healthy by trained health professionals according to strict clinical criteria.
evidence: This describes the participant selection criteria.

claim: Clustering by cell types was stronger than by age in principal component analysis of normalized DNA methylation data.
source: The PCA showed that clustering by cell types was stronger than by age (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from PCA analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The genes associated with the top 500 probes corresponding to PC1, PC2, and PC3 were enriched pathways linked to innate and adaptive lineage development.
source: The genes associated with the top 500 probes corresponding to PC1, PC2, and PC3 were enriched pathways linked to innate and adaptive lineage development (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a finding from pathway enrichment analysis of principal components.

claim: The number of hypo- or hypermethylated sites varied considerably between cell types.
source: The number of hypo- or hypermethylated sites varied considerably between cell types (Figure 1B) with highest numbers in CD4+ T cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and Supplementary files 3 and 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B and supplementary figures.

claim: CD4+ T cells had the highest numbers of age-associated methylation sites.
source: The number of hypo- or hypermethylated sites varied considerably between cell types (Figure 1B) with highest numbers in CD4+ T cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and Supplementary files 3 and 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B and supplementary figures.

claim: Using a comparison between young (≤35 years, 25th percentile) and old (≥70 years, 75th percentile) individuals, there was >90% overlap with beta-regression-derived hypomethylated sites in all cell types except CD8+ T cells.
source: Using a different approach of comparing between young (≤35 years, 25th percentile) and old (≥70 years, 75th percentile) individuals, we observed >90% overlap with beta-regression-derived hypomethylated sites and 70–95% overlap with hypermethylated sites in all cell types except CD8+ T cells (9–14% overlap) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing two different analytical approaches shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Using a comparison between young and old individuals, there was 70–95% overlap with beta-regression-derived hypermethylated sites in all cell types except CD8+ T cells.
source: Using a different approach of comparing between young (≤35 years, 25th percentile) and old (≥70 years, 75th percentile) individuals, we observed >90% overlap with beta-regression-derived hypomethylated sites and 70–95% overlap with hypermethylated sites in all cell types except CD8+ T cells (9–14% overlap) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing two different analytical approaches shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: CD8+ T cells showed only 9–14% overlap between young vs old comparison and beta-regression-derived age-associated sites.
source: Using a different approach of comparing between young (≤35 years, 25th percentile) and old (≥70 years, 75th percentile) individuals, we observed >90% overlap with beta-regression-derived hypomethylated sites and 70–95% overlap with hypermethylated sites in all cell types except CD8+ T cells (9–14% overlap) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing two different analytical approaches shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Having fewer old donors with CD8+ T cells may have contributed to differences in overlap between analytical approaches.
source: Having fewer old donors with CD8+ T cells may have contributed to differences (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is speculation about the reason for the CD8+ T cell differences.

claim: A significant proportion of age-hypomethylated CpGs were in the intergenic and open sea (>4 kb from CpG island) regions.
source: Like other studies, we found that a significant proportion of age-hypomethylated CpGs were in the intergenic and open sea (>4 kb from CpG island) regions while age-hypermethylated CpGs were in promoters and CpG islands (Chi sq test p < 0.001) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is a finding from genomic location analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E with statistical significance.

claim: Age-hypermethylated CpGs were in promoters and CpG islands.
source: Like other studies, we found that a significant proportion of age-hypomethylated CpGs were in the intergenic and open sea (>4 kb from CpG island) regions while age-hypermethylated CpGs were in promoters and CpG islands (Chi sq test p < 0.001) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is a finding from genomic location analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E with statistical significance.

claim: Age-associated differentially methylated sites in PBMC poorly recapitulate age-dependent changes that take place in specific primary immune cells.
source: Additionally, age-associated differentially methylated sites in PBMC poorly recapitulate age-dependent changes that take place in specific primary immune cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing PBMC with specific cell types shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E, F.

claim: Only 181 age-associated hypomethylated sites and 169 hypermethylated sites were shared between all 6 cell types.
source: Only 181 age-associated hypomethylated sites and 169 hypermethylated sites were shared between all 6 cell types.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the overlap analysis.

claim: The number of shared age-associated sites increased to 776 (age-hypomethylated) and 404 (age-hypermethylated) sites in 5 or more cell types.
source: These numbers increased to 776 (age-hypomethylated) and 404 (age-hypermethylated) sites in 5 or more cell types (Figure 1C, D).
evidence: This is a finding from the overlap analysis shown in Figure 1C, D.

claim: Most age-related methylation changes are cell specific.
source: Thus, most age-related methylation changes are cell specific.
evidence: This is an inference from the finding that only a small number of sites are shared across all cell types.

claim: Only 10 of the shared age-associated sites overlap with the 359 CpGs in Horvath's pan-tissue epigenetic clock.
source: Of note, only 10 of the sites overlap with the 359 CpGs in Horvath's pan-tissue epigenetic clock (Horvath, 2013).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing the study's results with Horvath's epigenetic clock.

claim: The poor overlap with Horvath's clock can be attributed to use of methylation array with about 21,369 CpGs for development of the clock in contrast to analyses based on ~850,000 CpG sites in this study.
source: Several reasons can be attributed to this poor overlap including (1) use of methylation array with about 21,369 CpGs for development of the clock in contrast to the analyses in this study based on ~850,000 CpG sites; (2) use of data from peripheral or whole blood for development these clocks in contrast to data from flow-sorted circulating immune cells in this study.
evidence: This is speculation about reasons for the poor overlap with Horvath's clock.

claim: The poor overlap with Horvath's clock can be attributed to use of data from peripheral or whole blood for development of the clock in contrast to data from flow-sorted circulating immune cells in this study.
source: Several reasons can be attributed to this poor overlap including (1) use of methylation array with about 21,369 CpGs for development of the clock in contrast to the analyses in this study based on ~850,000 CpG sites; (2) use of data from peripheral or whole blood for development these clocks in contrast to data from flow-sorted circulating immune cells in this study.
evidence: This is speculation about reasons for the poor overlap with Horvath's clock.

claim: The number of shared age-hypo- or hypermethylated CpGs across cells was significantly much higher than that expected based on chance alone.
source: While the number of shared age-hypo- or hypermethylated CpGs across cells was relatively small, it was significantly much higher than that expected based on chance alone, suggesting that common underlying epigenetic mechanisms exist across the considered cell types (Figure 1C, D).
evidence: This is a finding from statistical analysis shown in Figure 1C, D.

claim: Common underlying epigenetic mechanisms exist across the considered cell types.
source: While the number of shared age-hypo- or hypermethylated CpGs across cells was relatively small, it was significantly much higher than that expected based on chance alone, suggesting that common underlying epigenetic mechanisms exist across the considered cell types (Figure 1C, D).
evidence: This is an inference from the finding that shared sites are more common than expected by chance.

claim: CpG sites adjacent to RCAN1 (calcineurin 1) show similar age-associated patterns in all cell types.
source: For example, CpG sites adjacent to RCAN1 (calcineurin 1) and KLF14 (Krϋppel-Like Factor 14) show similar age-associated patterns in all cell types (Figure 1E, F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1E.

claim: CpG sites adjacent to KLF14 (Krϋppel-Like Factor 14) show similar age-associated patterns in all cell types.
source: For example, CpG sites adjacent to RCAN1 (calcineurin 1) and KLF14 (Krϋppel-Like Factor 14) show similar age-associated patterns in all cell types (Figure 1E, F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1F.

claim: THSD4 and CCDC102B were the most significant age-associated hypomethylated genes shared by five or more cell types.
source: THSD4 and CCDC102B were the most significant age-associated hypomethylated genes shared by five or more cell types, while ELOVL2, KLF14, LHFP14, and GPR158 were among the most significant age-hypermethylated genes in five or more cell types.
evidence: This is a finding from analyzing the top age-associated genes.

claim: ELOVL2, KLF14, LHFP14, and GPR158 were among the most significant age-hypermethylated genes in five or more cell types.
source: THSD4 and CCDC102B were the most significant age-associated hypomethylated genes shared by five or more cell types, while ELOVL2, KLF14, LHFP14, and GPR158 were among the most significant age-hypermethylated genes in five or more cell types.
evidence: This is a finding from analyzing the top age-associated genes.

claim: Only 13–15% of the 'top' age-associated probes overlapped with the list of age-associated probes shared across cell types.
source: It is noteworthy that only 13–15% of these 'top' age-associated probes overlapped with the list of age-associated probes shared across cell types (181 hypomethylated and 169 hypermethylated probes).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing top probes with shared probes.

claim: Most CpGs with age-associated methylation consistent across cell types undergo moderate (although significant) methylation changes with aging.
source: These findings suggest that most CpGs with age-associated methylation consistent across cell types undergo moderate (although significant) methylation changes with aging.
evidence: This is an inference from the finding that top probes don't overlap much with shared probes.

claim: Of the 181 hypomethylated and 169 hypermethylated CpGs with age in all cell types in GESTALT, 72 and 135, respectively, were represented in the 450K microarray used in the InCHIANTI study.
source: Of the 181 hypomethylated and 169 hypermethylated CpGs with age in all cell types in GESTALT, 72 and 135, respectively, were represented in the 450K microarray (Moore et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the overlap between the two studies' platforms.

claim: The beta-coefficients for age of the 207 CpG probes estimated from the GESTALT study and their corresponding values estimated longitudinally from the InCHIANTI study were highly and significantly correlated.
source: The beta-coefficients for age of the 207 CpG probes (72 + 135) estimated from the GESTALT study and their corresponding values estimated longitudinally from the InCHIANTI study were highly and significantly correlated (hypomethylated with age CpGs: r = 0.49, p = 1.2e−09 and hypermethylated with age CpGs: r = 0.5, p = 6.9e−06 for average beta coefficients across six cell types, Figure 2C, D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from correlation analysis shown in Figure 2C, D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: For hypomethylated with age CpGs, the correlation between GESTALT and InCHIANTI beta-coefficients was r = 0.49, p = 1.2e−09.
source: The beta-coefficients for age of the 207 CpG probes (72 + 135) estimated from the GESTALT study and their corresponding values estimated longitudinally from the InCHIANTI study were highly and significantly correlated (hypomethylated with age CpGs: r = 0.49, p = 1.2e−09 and hypermethylated with age CpGs: r = 0.5, p = 6.9e−06 for average beta coefficients across six cell types, Figure 2C, D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statistical result from correlation analysis.

claim: For hypermethylated with age CpGs, the correlation between GESTALT and InCHIANTI beta-coefficients was r = 0.5, p = 6.9e−06.
source: The beta-coefficients for age of the 207 CpG probes (72 + 135) estimated from the GESTALT study and their corresponding values estimated longitudinally from the InCHIANTI study were highly and significantly correlated (hypomethylated with age CpGs: r = 0.49, p = 1.2e−09 and hypermethylated with age CpGs: r = 0.5, p = 6.9e−06 for average beta coefficients across six cell types, Figure 2C, D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statistical result from correlation analysis.

claim: CpGs identified as differentially methylated with aging across cell types in GESTALT also change longitudinally with aging.
source: Thus, CpGs identified as differentially methylated with aging across cell types in GESTALT also change longitudinally with aging.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the correlation analysis with InCHIANTI data.

claim: Several CpGs showed significant but opposing age trends in different cell types, especially in B, CD4+ T cells, and monocytes.
source: Several CpGs showed significant but opposing age trends in different cell types, especially in B, CD4+ T cells, and monocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G).
evidence: This is a finding shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, G.

claim: cg27123256 in the gene body of BCL11B was age hypomethylated in non-T cells and significantly age hypermethylated in naive CD4+ T cells.
source: For example, cg27123256 in the gene body of BCL11B was age hypomethylated in non-T cells and significantly age hypermethylated in naive CD4+ T cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The observations implicate BCL11B in aging-related changes in naive CD4+ T cell function, distinct from its proposed role in effector cells.
source: Our observations implicate BCL11B in aging-related changes in naive CD4+ T cell function, distinct from its proposed role in effector cells (Tserel et al., 2015; Gray et al., 2014; Yui and Rothenberg, 2014).
evidence: This is an inference from the BCL11B methylation pattern, with citations to previous work on BCL11B.

claim: cg03530364 in the body of FAM19A1 gene was hypermethylated in non-T cells but age-hypomethylated in CD4+ T cells.
source: Conversely, cg03530364 in the body of FAM19A1 gene was hypermethylated in non-T cells but age-hypomethylated in CD4+ T cells (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2F.

claim: None of the CpGs with opposite age-methylation trends in specific cell types were differentially age-methylated in PBMC.
source: Of note, none of these CpGs were differentially age-methylated in PBMC.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing cell-specific results with PBMC.

claim: Opposite age-methylation trends in specific cell types may cancel each other and obscure their relevance for aging when mixed cell-type samples are assessed.
source: Thus, opposite age-methylation trends in specific cell types may cancel each other and obscure their relevance for aging when mixed cell-type samples are assessed.
evidence: This is an inference from the finding that opposite trends in specific cells are not detected in PBMC.

claim: Gene set enrichment analyses identified 30 pathways (q-value <0.05) associated with age-associated genes.
source: Gene set enrichment analyses were performed on genes associated with at least one CpG significantly age-hypo- or hypermethylated in five or more cell types. We identified 30 pathways (q-value <0.05) (Figure 3 and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is a finding from pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Probes commonly age-hypomethylated in five or more cell types (n = 776) pointed to genes enriched in collagen biosynthesis, complement cascade, and GTPase pathways.
source: Probes commonly age-hypomethylated in five or more cell types (n = 776) pointed to genes enriched in collagen biosynthesis, complement cascade, and GTPase pathways (left-most column in bottom panel of Figure 3) that highlighted inflammatory and metabolic pathway in aging.
evidence: This is a finding from pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Genes associated with shared age-hypermethylated probes (n = 404) were enriched for neural pathways previously implicated to brain aging along with G-protein-coupled receptors pathways.
source: Genes associated with shared age-hypermethylated probes (n = 404) were enriched for neural pathways previously implicated to brain aging along with G-protein-coupled receptors pathways (de Oliveira et al., 2019; Ewing et al., 2019) (left-most column in top panel of Figure 3).
evidence: This is a finding from pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3, with citations to previous work.

claim: A recent study by Karagiannis et al. also identified neuronal genes in their PBMC aging data emphasizing a possible interlink between immune-aging and neuronal pathways.
source: A recent study by Karagiannis et al. also identified neuronal genes in their PBMC aging data emphasizing a possible interlink between immune-aging and neuronal pathways (Karagiannis et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Karagiannis et al., 2023.

claim: Age-associated hypomethylated CpGs were significantly enriched for weak/active enhancers.
source: Age-associated hypomethylated CpGs were significantly enriched for weak/active enhancers (yellow bar, Figure 4A) whereas, confirming previous reports, age-hypermethylated CpGs, were enriched in bivalent/polycomb regions compared to control set (brown and dark gray bars, respectively, in Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from chromHMM annotation shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Age-hypermethylated CpGs were enriched in bivalent/polycomb regions compared to control set.
source: Age-associated hypomethylated CpGs were significantly enriched for weak/active enhancers (yellow bar, Figure 4A) whereas, confirming previous reports, age-hypermethylated CpGs, were enriched in bivalent/polycomb regions compared to control set (brown and dark gray bars, respectively, in Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from chromHMM annotation shown in Figure 4A, confirming previous reports.

claim: A V-shaped peak-valley-peak pattern of DNase hypersensitivity was observed at sites of age-associated hypomethylation in B and CD4+ T cells, which is characteristic of promoter sites.
source: For B and CD4+ T cells, we observed a V-shaped peak-valley-peak pattern of DNase hypersensitivity at sites of age-associated hypomethylation, which is characteristic of promoter sites (Figure 4C; Pundhir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from DNase hypersensitivity analysis shown in Figure 4C, with citation to Pundhir et al., 2016.

claim: Both age-associated hypo- and hypermethylated sites showed evident H3K4me1 peaks, a marker commonly associated with active and primed enhancers.
source: Both age-associated hypo- and hypermethylated sites showed evident H3K4me1 peaks, a marker commonly associated with active and primed enhancers (Figure 4C; Bae and Lesch, 2020).
evidence: This is a finding from histone mark analysis shown in Figure 4C, with citation to Bae and Lesch, 2020.

claim: No specific trend was observed for H3K4me3 and H3K27ac.
source: No specific trend was observed for H3K4me3 and H3K27ac (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from histone mark analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The patterns of chromatin accessibility and histone marks were highly consistent across cell types.
source: These patterns were highly consistent across cell types (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and strongly suggest a functional connection between methylation and chromatin status.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing patterns across cell types shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The patterns of chromatin accessibility and histone marks strongly suggest a functional connection between methylation and chromatin status.
source: These patterns were highly consistent across cell types (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and strongly suggest a functional connection between methylation and chromatin status.
evidence: This is an inference from the consistent patterns observed.

claim: The DHS and histone data in the ENCODE database were only available for either one of two donors (a 21-year-old male and 37-year-old female).
source: However, as the DHS and histone data in the ENCODE database were only available for either one of two donors (a 21-year-old male and 37-year-old female), we could not verify whether the patterns observed are stable with change in age.
evidence: This is a limitation of the analysis stated in the text.

claim: The binding motif for aryl hydrocarbon receptor nuclear translocator (ARNT, also named HIF1β) was associated with age-hypomethylated CpGs across most cell types.
source: We observed that the binding motif for aryl hydrocarbon receptor nuclear translocator (ARNT, also named HIF1β) was associated with age-hypomethylated CpGs across most cell types (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from HOMER TF motif analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The only exception to ARNT enrichment in age-hypomethylated CpGs was naive CD8+ T cells where the top enriched motif was B-cell lymphoma gene 6 (BCL6).
source: The only exception was naive CD8+ T cells where the top enriched motif was B-cell lymphoma gene 6 (BCL6).
evidence: This is a finding from HOMER TF motif analysis.

claim: BCL6 codes for a zinc finger TF that plays a critical role in the generation of memory and effector cells in acute infection.
source: BCL6 code for a zinc finger TF that plays a critical role in the generation of memory and effector cells in acute infection (Kim et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kim et al., 2020.

claim: Another motif associated with age-hypomethylated CpGs across most cell types was chromatin architectural protein CTCF and its closely related gene BORIS.
source: Another motif associated with age-hypomethylated CpGs across most cell types was chromatin architectural protein CTCF and its closely related gene BORIS.
evidence: This is a finding from HOMER TF motif analysis.

claim: Methylation changes at CTCF sites have been reported to reflect large-scale genome reorganization in immune cells in older individuals.
source: Methylation changes at CTCF sites have been reported to reflect large-scale genome reorganization in immune cells in older individuals (van Ruiten and Rowland, 2021; Bhat et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to van Ruiten and Rowland, 2021 and Bhat et al., 2021.

claim: Repressor Element 1-Silencing Transcription Factor (REST) was the TF motif most frequently associated with age-hypermethylated CpGs in five of six cell types.
source: Repressor Element 1-Silencing Transcription Factor (REST) was the TF motifs most frequently associated with age-hypermethylated CpGs in five of six cell types (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from HOMER TF motif analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Age-hypermethylated sites in PBMCs have been previously shown to be enriched for REST, which is known to repress stress response genes and is lost in cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease pathology.
source: Age-hypermethylated sites in PBMCs have been previously shown to be enriched for REST, which is known to repress stress response genes and is lost in cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease pathology (Yuan et al., 2015; Lu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yuan et al., 2015 and Lu et al., 2014.

claim: The top enriched TF motif associated with age-hypermethylated sites in monocytes was Arid5A (p < 10−27).
source: The top enriched TF motif associated with age-hypermethylated sites in monocytes was Arid5A (p < 10−27) that binds to selective inflammation-related genes, such as IL6 and STAT3 and stabilize their expression (Nyati et al., 2020; Wilsker et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a finding from HOMER TF motif analysis with statistical significance.

claim: Arid5A binds to selective inflammation-related genes, such as IL6 and STAT3 and stabilizes their expression.
source: The top enriched TF motif associated with age-hypermethylated sites in monocytes was Arid5A (p < 10−27) that binds to selective inflammation-related genes, such as IL6 and STAT3 and stabilize their expression (Nyati et al., 2020; Wilsker et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nyati et al., 2020 and Wilsker et al., 2002.

claim: When the analysis was repeated with a smaller 50 bp window size for TF motif search, motifs for ARNT, CTCF, and REST remained the top hits in most cell types.
source: We further repeated the analysis with a smaller 50 bp window size for TF motif search. Motifs for ARNT, CTCF, and REST remained the top hits in most cell types (Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is a finding from repeating the HOMER analysis with different parameters.

source: ARNT is the beta subunit of Hypoxia Factor 1 (HIF-1), which is stabilized during hypoxia and shuttled to the nucleus where it binds to DNA hypoxia-response elements and triggers a complex response that include upregulation of angiogenesis and erythropoiesis and reprogramming of energetic metabolism from oxidative phosphorylation to anaerobic glycolysis (Semenza, 2000).

claim: HIF-1 triggers a complex response that includes upregulation of angiogenesis and erythropoiesis and reprogramming of energetic metabolism from oxidative phosphorylation to anaerobic glycolysis.
